utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-99-36-T, The Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: David Cunningham with John Ackerman, assisted by Aleksandar Vujic, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you all. I understand there are some preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I start this morning, I was waiting till Mr. Ackerman to return to the Court, although in fact in a sense it's not something that he can have much of a say because it affects him. It deals with the question of the contempt hearing against the Defence attorney as she was then, Milka Maglov. Your Honour will recall that during the hearing which I observed, Ms. Hollis who has been instructed as amicus by the registry raised the question of whether or not the composition of the Trial Chamber should be the same as for the trial. And Your Honour, in essence, I'm raising it now in the presence of Mr. Brdjanin and Defence counsel for this reason: Your Honours have ordered that the hearing be held, effectively still during the course of the trial against Radoslav Brdjanin. Your Honours, aside from the fact whether it perhaps is a matter that in any event should be dealt with by another Trial Chamber, although I know in my jurisdiction, a contempt in the face of a court is dealt with certainly in the first place by the Judge. Your Honour, here the facts are slightly different, and the problem is one that I wish to before Your Honours, that it's quite plain that Mr. Ackerman will be a witness. Ms. Hollis raised, I think, the question of whether in fact she might call him. Ms. Maglov made no bones about it. She intends to call Mr. Ackerman as a witness. And Your Honours, what that does is raise, in our respectful submission, a difficulty in that Your Honours may find yourselves in the position of having to assess the quality of Mr. Ackerman's evidence whilst he is still appearing in front of you as Defence counsel. Your Honours, in those circumstances, it seems to me that it may put everyone in an embarrassing position, both Your Honours and Mr. Ackerman himself. Your Honours, our respectful submission is that could have an effect, could, and I say no more than that, at a later stage, once this trial is completed, or even possibly whilst the trial is still going on. And Your Honours, what we would respectfully ask - because in this the Prosecution does have an interest - is either that this matter be, if the date is to be retained, that it be heard by a different Trial Chamber or a different composition of Trial Chamber II, or alternatively, that the matter be adjourned until the conclusion of the proceedings in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Do you have any comments, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be inappropriate for me to say very much because of my witness status. But I -- it has occurred to me that if the Brdjanin trial is still ongoing at the time this hearing is held, I might very well have a right to assert a privilege against testifying based on work product and matters of that nature which would not exist if the trial were over. And I have not consulted anyone regarding that other than my own brain. But it could create a serious problem, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, we will take what you have both stated into consideration, and we will take a decision in due course. But I might as well inform you that in the past month or so, there was -- there were steps taken to have the case -- the contempt case transferred to another Chamber again, the second time I tried that. And it was returned back to us, and not only that, but another contempt case that we were going to be seized with has been referred back to the same. So there is a policy going on. I do read you out loud and clear, Ms. Korner. Don't misunderstand me. I do not share your preoccupations, and that I can say without hesitation. I don't -- I'm not really worried about what you are worried or what you are concerned with. I am more concerned with what Mr. Ackerman has just mentioned now because that, indeed, could create a problem for whoever tries to produce him or bring him forward as a witness. But anyway, these may well be pleasures yet to come. But we'll think about what you have stated and we will take a decision. Thank you. Anything else before -- yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I owe the Chamber an apology because I didn't deliver an exhibit list. What I've tried to do, and done, is made copies of the exhibits that I'm going to use and distributed them to the Registrar. So I apologise to the Chamber about that. With respect to witnesses, we had planned for Witness number 11 to be here this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That witness is not testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: We believe that based on the representations made by the OTP, that the witnesses we have scheduled which are 40, 63, and 64 will take us through the end of the business day on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Cunningham. Let's go into closed session. We'll bring the witness in and we'll see whether it's the case of confirming the protective measures that we have granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of December, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
